children: Bosch share price: Shares of Bosch Ltd declined 4 percent to Rs 50,375 in afternoon trade on Friday, after the company announced a stock split and a bonus share issue alongside its Q2 FY27 financial results. The company reported an 18.6 percent year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 839.4 crore, supported by strong revenue growth.
The Bosch board approved a 1:5 stock split, under which each existing equity share with a face value of Rs 10 will be subdivided into five equity shares with a face value of Rs 2 each.

In addition, the board approved a 3:1 bonus share issue, under which shareholders will receive three bonus equity shares for every one equity share held after the stock split. Both proposals are subject to shareholder approval through a postal ballot.
Bosch stock split and bonus issue details

Under the proposed stock split, one fully paid-up equity share of Rs 10 face value will be subdivided into five fully paid-up equity shares of Rs 2 face value each. Following the subdivision, Bosch plans to issue three bonus equity shares of Rs 2 face value for every one existing equity share of Rs 2 face value.

Taken together, the two corporate actions mean that one existing Bosch share will translate into 20 shares after the stock split and bonus issue, subject to the necessary approvals.

Bosch reported an 18.6 percent increase in net profit to Rs 839.4 crore for the July-September quarter, compared with Rs 708 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The quarterly results included a one-time gain of Rs 130 crore. Revenue rose 28.2 percent year-on-year to Rs 7,655 crore from Rs 5,969 crore in the year-ago period.

According to the company's investor presentation, revenue from operations grew 28.2 percent sequentially, driven by strong demand in passenger cars, four-wheel-drive vehicles and two-wheelers, favourable product mix and pre-festive demand. Robust e-commerce and accessory sales also supported growth in the consumer goods business.

Bosch's mobility business recorded sequential growth of 29.8 percent, led by a 36.4 percent increase in Power Solutions and a 34.9 percent rise in Vehicle Motion. Mobility Aftermarket grew 13.2 percent, while the two-wheeler segment expanded 17.7 percent. The consumer goods segment registered growth of 17.1 percent.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 23.2 percent to Rs 1,037 crore, compared with Rs 842 crore a year earlier. Bosch attributed the sequential increase in EBITDA primarily to higher revenue, partly offset by increased raw material costs. However, EBITDA margin narrowed to 13.5 percent from 14 percent in the corresponding quarter last year, despite strong revenue and operating earnings growth.
